strengths: Rigorous theoretical framework (SAM) that unifies multiple bias mechanisms (confounders, colliders, mediators) under causal graphical analysis with formal proofs of conditional independence ensuring causal stability

Novel and elegant algorithmic contributions: DISCOm and sDISCO provide computationally efficient alternatives to previously impractical conditional distance correlation implementations, with sDISCO offering a single-shot global approach

Comprehensive and fair experimental evaluation across five diverse datasets with thoughtful hyperparameter budgets, clear acknowledgment of baselines' complexity, and beyond-standard evaluation using pathway-specific counterfactual analysis
Practical advantages: methods support arbitrary variable type combinations, scale seamlessly to multi-bias scenarios, and require substantially fewer hyperparameters than competitors (HSCIC, CIRCE)
Rigorous mathematical treatment with detailed proofs, proper structural causal model formalism, and careful treatment of Hilbert space embeddings for distance covariance theory
weaknesses: Limited theoretical novelty: SAM framework substantially adapts Plecko & Bareinboim (2022) without fundamental innovation; conditional independence criterion Ŷ ⊥ B | Y has been used empirically in prior work; Theorem 1 is somewhat incremental

Critical assumptions are strong and under-validated: anti-causal prediction (Y→X) limits applicability; no unobserved confounders assumption is rarely satisfied; Section 2.2's treatment of violations is superficial with only brief empirical validation (Figure 4a) and no principled mitigation strategies

Mixed and marginal experimental results undermining main claims: sDISCO (0.619) worse than CIRCE (0.606) on dSprites; CIRCE (0.894) substantially outperforms sDISCO (0.863, -3.1%) on Waterbirds; DISCOm worse than GDRO on YaleB (-0.036); improvements often within standard deviations without significance testing

Gap between theory and practice not adequately addressed: Theorem 1 requires Ŷ ⊥ W,Z | Y but practical regularization (Eq. 24) only enforces Ŷ ⊥ B | Y; no empirical analysis of how well optimization achieves theoretical guarantees or finite-sample convergence behavior

Insufficient failure analysis and limited scope: counterfactual analysis restricted to dSprites; no ablation studies on kernel choice/bandwidth/m parameter; missing explanations for CIRCE's Waterbirds superiority; only 5 datasets, mostly controlled; problematic FairFace operationalization acknowledged but not addressed

Missing critical details: no computational complexity analysis or runtime comparisons; no sensitivity analysis to bandwidth hyperparameter σ_Y; no statistical significance testing; hyperparameter ranges in Table 3 appear arbitrary; robustness to anti-causal assumption not systematically tested on real data

Incomplete related work and justification: relationship to Invariant Risk Minimization underdeveloped; fairness metrics entirely absent despite fairness implications; distance correlation advantage over HSIC not empirically demonstrated (HSCIC performs comparably on several datasets)

strengths: Well-motivated causal framework (SAM) that elegantly unifies different bias mechanisms (confounders, colliders, mediators) with rigorous derivation of conditional independence criterion Ŷ ⊥ B | Y
Significant practical innovation: DISCOm and sDISCO overcome computational bottlenecks in conditional distance correlation, making it practical for deep learning optimization
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across five datasets with thoughtful protocol (including fair hyperparameter budgets giving competitors even more tuning runs)
Insightful pathway-specific counterfactual analysis (Section 4.4) revealing important trade-offs that standard metrics miss—e.g., HSCIC/CIRCE sacrificing target information while debiasing
Honest treatment of limitations: clearly discusses unobserved confounding gap between theory and practice, validated experimentally with partial bias knowledge
Strong reproducibility: detailed hyperparameter grids, explicit implementation details, reproducibility statement, consistent fairness in baseline comparisons
weaknesses: Limited theoretical novelty: SAM builds heavily on Plecko & Bareinboim (2022), and the conditional independence criterion has prior empirical use in fairness literature (Makar & D'Amour 2022, Kaur et al. 2022); distinction from prior work could be clearer
Conditional distance correlation concept not novel—prior work by Wang et al. (2015) and Póczos & Schneider (2012); contribution is primarily operational (efficiency), not conceptual

Significant theory-practice gap: theoretical guarantees assume no unobserved confounders (Z' = ∅), but real applications have unobserved confounding; no guidance provided on acceptable levels of unobserved bias

Modest empirical improvements over baselines: DISCOm/sDISCO are competitive but not consistently superior (CIRCE wins on Waterbirds); main advantage is simpler hyperparameter tuning (2 vs 5+ parameters) rather than predictive power
Experimental scope limited to vision datasets (all relatively controlled/small); no evaluation on NLP, tabular, or other modalities raises generalization questions

Practical applicability concerns: requires knowing bias variables B in advance with no principled discovery method; kernel bandwidth σ_Y still requires tuning; O(n²) distance matrix computation cost not analyzed for large-scale data
Limited discussion of when anti-causal assumption is appropriate, how to validate SAM assumptions in practice, or relationship to invariance-based approaches (IRM, etc.)
Missing ablation studies, wall-clock timing comparisons showing actual speedup over Wang et al. (2015), and sensitivity analysis to kernel choices beyond RBF

strengths: Solid theoretical foundation: SAM framework elegantly unifies three bias mechanisms through causal pathway analysis with rigorous mathematical grounding (Theorems 2.3-2.4, Proposition 2.1)

Non-trivial computational innovation: sDISCO's O(n²) factorization (Theorem G.1) genuinely solves the O(n³) bottleneck of conditional distance correlation, making it practical for deep learning for the first time

Comprehensive and fair experimental evaluation: 6 diverse datasets, 7 strong baselines with careful hyperparameter allocation, multiple runs with error bars, counterfactual validation on controlled dSprites data

Flexibility and generality: Handles arbitrary combinations of target/bias types (continuous/categorical) and scales to multi-bias scenarios, outperforming specialized methods (GDRO, IRM) in capability

Transparent treatment of limitations: Clear discussion of SAM assumption violations (positivity, unobserved confounding), honest acknowledgment of implementation errors and corrections, thoughtful ethical considerations for sensitive datasets
weaknesses: Incremental empirical improvements: sDISCO ranks 1st or 2nd on datasets but differences often within standard deviations; CIRCE outperforms substantially on Waterbirds (0.894 vs 0.874). Gains do not justify complexity relative to simpler baselines like GDRO

Limited practical applicability: Requires observed and labeled bias variables during training (informed regime only). No practical diagnostics provided to verify whether SAM structure holds for a given application. Selective mediation exception requires prior knowledge that may not exist

Validation concerns: Implementation errors discovered in sDISCO that 'propagated into code' raise rigor questions. Ground-truth counterfactual validation only on synthetic dSprites; real-world validation of causal stability is missing. Most datasets are synthetic or heavily controlled

Incomplete guidance for practitioners: Bandwidth σ_Y selection not principled (grid search only). No discussion of sensitivity to batch size, initialization, or numerical stability. Unobserved confounding discussion offers little comfort—no guidance on when to worry about proxy variables masking hidden confounders

Theoretical limitations incompletely addressed: Positivity assumption can be restrictive in practice. When unobserved confounders Z' exist without proxies in X, the method fails but no diagnostics provided. Counterfactual analysis in Section 4.4 only demonstrated on synthetic data where ground truth exists

strengths: Novel theoretical framework (SAM) providing unified causal characterization of three bias types with rigorous mathematical decomposition into stable/indirect/spurious effects

Clever computational contribution (sDISCO): exact algebraic factorization reducing memory from O(n³) to O(n²) via diagonal extraction identity, enabling practical conditional distance correlation in deep learning
Rigorous theoretical analysis with complete proofs; principled approach to deriving observational criteria from causal structures
Honest and thorough discussion of assumption violations (Section 2.2) with clear statements about theoretical limitations and best-achievable guarantees under unobserved confounding
Thorough experimental evaluation across 6 diverse datasets (vision/NLP, synthetic/real) with fair hyperparameter treatment, including extensive appendices with reproducibility details
Flexibility to handle arbitrary combinations of target/bias variable types and multi-attribute bias scenarios, with significantly fewer hyperparameters than competing methods
Pathway-specific counterfactual analysis enabled by SAM framework, providing fine-grained insights into why models fail (Section 4.4, Appendix H.4)
Successful bridge between causal inference theory and practical deep learning optimization, with transparent disclosure of implementation corrections
weaknesses: Empirical results competitive rather than clearly superior: no consistent winner across datasets; DISCOm best on 2/6 datasets, sDISCO on 1/6; performance often within error bars of GDRO/CIRCE
Significant practical limitations understated: requires observed bias variables (unknown biases cannot be handled), limiting real-world applicability where relevant biases are often unknown a priori

Strong causal assumptions required for theoretical guarantees (no unobserved confounders, sufficient variability) are often violated in practice; paper provides limited empirical guidance on detecting/handling violations

Limited novelty in individual components: SAM extends Plecko & Bareinboim (2022) primarily to anti-causal setting; conditional distance correlation from Wang et al. (2015); independence criterion Ŷ ⊥ B | Y used empirically in prior work (Makar & D'Amour 2023)

Implementation reliability concerns: previous sDISCO version had mathematical/code discrepancies (Table 4 vs Table 2) discovered during refactoring; no accessible source code link provided despite reproducibility claims
Kernel bandwidth h selection poorly addressed: sensitivity analysis minimal, practical guidance for practitioners missing, unclear how to choose h in new problems

Dense presentation (30+ pages) with heavy counterfactual notation (ctf-stable, ctf-IE, ctf-SE) that, while precise, creates accessibility barrier; gap between theory (Section 2) and practical application (Eq. 19) is abrupt

No statistical significance testing between methods; while hyperparameter generosity to baselines is commendable, competitive results lack rigorous comparison; results on MNLI use different metric (WGA) reducing comparability
